name: Equifax
description: Equifax is one of the three US credit bureaus: lenders pay it per credit report and score, and mortgage lenders buy 'tri-merge' reports that combine Equifax, Experian and TransUnion data. Its largest and most profitable business, Workforce Solutions (The Work Number), earns fees from lenders, landlords and employers for instantly verifying income and employment from payroll data it collects from employers; it earns about 63 percent of segment profit from 43 percent of revenue. It also sells credit data internationally and consumer products. Mortgage activity (credit inquiries) is a major driver of both US segments.

employees.note: About 15,000 employees in 22 countries (about 3,100 in Workforce Solutions).

businessLines.name: Workforce Solutions
businessLines.how: Per-lookup fees from lenders, landlords, government agencies and screeners to verify an applicant's income and employment against payroll records that employers supply; plus employer-side services (tax credits, unemployment claims, I-9 and onboarding) sold to employers per transaction or per contract.

businessLines.name: U.S. Information Solutions (USIS)
businessLines.how: Per-report and per-score fees from lenders and other businesses buying consumer and commercial credit information, decisioning tools and mortgage tri-merge reports (volume follows credit inquiries and mortgage originations), plus fees for marketing lists and portfolio analytics.

businessLines.name: International
businessLines.how: Same credit-information model as the US, fees per report, score and analytics product sold to lenders and businesses in Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Canada, plus consumer products.

brands.name: The Work Number
brands.note: Employment and income verification database within Workforce Solutions (product name not broken out in revenue in the 10-K text reviewed)
